The Hebrew has an idiom, "to lift up the face," or "distinguish the face," that is used to convey meaning with respect to or showing partiality to a person. For example in Leviticus 19:15 we find the following in the Hebrew text: ... thou shalt not lift up the faces of the poor.... This expression is rendered by the Authorized Version: ... thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, ... The meaning of this is shown by the next clause, "nor honor the person of the mighty," ... That is to say, no partiality was to be shown.
quotes.attr: Hebrew Idioms in the Book of Mormon by Dr. Sidney B. Sperry, Improvement Era, 1954, Vol. Lvii. October, 1954. No. 10

quotes.text: The Savior also commanded individuals to be judges, both of circumstances and of other people. Through the prophet Moses, the Lord commanded Israel, "Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment: thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty: but in righteousness shalt thou judge thy neighbour" (Leviticus 19:15).
quotes.speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
quotes.attr: Dallin H. Oaks, "Judge Not and Judging", CES Fireside, 1 March 1998
